ORV FINAL ENVIRONMENTAL STATEMENT (INT FES )
APPENDIX
Introduction to Interior Analysis and Disposition Made of Comments Received
In response to the request for public comments on the Department's draft ORV environmental statement (INT DES 72-62), more than 300 pages of comments were received from 144 organizations, agencies, and private citizens. Included were comments from 7 Federal agencies, in addition to those from bureaus within the Department of the Interior. Also, comments were received from departmental and executive offices of 33 States and the District of Columbia, 38 private organizations, and 44 private citizens.
The responses received from the 38 private organizations can be broken down into five categories: ORV user groups (8); mining and geophysical exploration groups (11); conservation and environmental groups (13); industry (4); and colleges and universities (2).
Appended Table 1 has the responses listed by name, date and number of pages, and whether from Federal, State, or local governmental agency, or private organization or individual. These responses have been filed by chronological date and given the numbers 1 through 116 and are filed in the Appendix to this statement. These numbers are stamped in the lower left hand corner of each page. Thus, the first response was received from the State of Wyoming, Executive Department, and was dated 6/12/72; it was given the number "1" and filed as the first page in these responses. The second response was from the American Motorcycle Association, and was dated 6/21/72; it was given the number "2" and filed after response number "1." Thus, the sequence for numbering and filing all responses. Response #91, dated 8/3/72, consists of the signatures of 29 Nevada residents, and adding these to the other 115 responses makes a total of 144 responses received.
Appended Table 2 provides a breakdown of the responses by types of agencies and individuals, listing the names of ORV user groups, mining and geophysical exploration groups, conservation and environmental groups, colleges and universities, and private citizens.
Federal Agency Comments
Comments on the draft ORV environmental statement were received from 7 other Federal agencies in addition to those received from the 7 bureaus within the Department of the Interior. The comments were quite helpful and they have been incorporated, as applicable, into the final environmental statement and the Departmental ORV regulations: In summary these comments were as follows:
#56 1. Department of Commerce, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Environmental Affairs - suggested that environmental statement, on page 12, lines 3 and 4, delineate those resources affected and to what degree by the proposed action; called our attention to 16 USC 478 which provides for access to public lands for purpose of prospecting;
